## Overview

Every contemporaneous mediation model measures the mediator and the outcome at the *same* wave (t2), so it cannot establish temporal precedence — the weakness the DAG's §12 flags and scopes to a wave-unrolled workstream (issue #250). Those models carry a t3 *sensitivity* (mediator at t2, outcome at t3). LRP76 promotes that ordering to the **primary** estimand and pushes the separation to the maximum the panel allows: the mediator (letter-sound knowledge $L$) stays at t2, the outcome (word reading $W$) is taken at **t4**, so the mediator strictly precedes the outcome by two waves. (The t3 sensitivity is skipped — it would double-lag.)

## Design

Mediator $L_{t2}$ (Beta-Binomial on $L_{t1}$); outcome $W_{t4}$ (conditioned on $W_{t1}$, loaded via the lagged-outcome preparation). Adjustment $\{G, A, E, R, W_\text{pre}, L_{t1}\}$ — identical to [LRP59](../lrp-rli-med-059).

## Assumptions — read this first {#sec-assumptions}

Assignment still randomises early-start versus delayed-start treatment schedules after crossover. It does not randomise letter-sound knowledge or identify the mediator–outcome relation. Measuring the mediator at t2 and the outcome at t4 establishes their measurement order, while latent ability and treatment-induced dose confounding still prevent a causal natural-effect interpretation. Read the decomposition under its stated forward model and compare it with the contemporaneous and t3-outcome analyses as a sensitivity to timing.
